items.text: Explain Formal Safety Assessment (FSA) and its application to Li-Ion battery fire risk.
items.reason: human review found the evidence does not settle this question: Formal Safety Assessment and its application to Li-ion battery fire risk. Genuinely two-limbed, and the limbs belong to different domains. FSA is the IMO five-step rulemaking risk methodology (HAZID, risk assessment, RCOs, GCAF cost-benefit, recommendations) -- note it is IMO-level regulatory development, not ISM shipboard management, so D03 is only a partial fit. The applied half is thermal runaway, CO2 ineffectiveness and the SOLAS II-2 amendments under MSC.520(106), which is D08. Which limb an examiner pursues is not knowable from the stem. Held rather than forced.

items.text: What ship certificates and documents relate to WHO (World Health Organization) requirements?
items.reason: human review found the evidence does not settle this question: WHO-related ship certificates. Two genuine limbs and no clean owner: the Ship Sanitation Control / Exemption Certificate is an IHR 2005 port-health certificate with its own validity and extension rules (D01 grammar), while the second half is seafarer medical fitness under ILO/WHO guidelines read through STCW and MLC (D03, and the card is authored with data-tags='mlc'). No MIW domain claims the public-health regime outright. Held rather than forced; the hold is count-neutral so D03 is unaffected.
